replacements.before:
Table~\ref{tab:process-dynamics} shows a mostly simple writing loop after repeat collapsing and leading-\texttt{Planning} reconstruction: 74.6\% of complete paths conform to the \texttt{Planning}--\texttt{Translating}--\texttt{Reviewing} cycle structure, while 14.8\% of runs return from \texttt{Reviewing} to \texttt{Translating}.
Full replanning (0.3\%) and goal replacement (\AfourRegenerationRate) are rare, so adaptivity is used mainly for targeted redrafting, consistent with the small exploratory advantage over \condFixedOrder\ because ordering can matter only when the controller departs from the common path.
replacements.after:
Table~\ref{tab:process-dynamics} shows a mostly simple writing loop after repeat collapsing and leading-\texttt{Planning} reconstruction: \AfourCycleCompliantRate\ of complete paths conform to the \texttt{Planning}--\texttt{Translating}--\texttt{Reviewing} cycle structure, while \AfourReviewingToTranslatingRate\ of runs return from \texttt{Reviewing} to \texttt{Translating}.
Full replanning (\AfourReviewingToPlanningRate) and goal replacement (\AfourRegenerationRate) are rare, so adaptivity is used mainly for targeted redrafting, consistent with the small exploratory advantage over \condFixedOrder\ because ordering can matter only when the controller departs from the common path.

\input{tab/appendix-process}

\paragraph{Trace processing.}
Process paths are read from the \texttt{Monitor}'s \texttt{process\_switch} events in trace order: each event's destination process is one step, and a run ends once, after its last step (E in Figure~\ref{fig:process-sequences}).
Figure~\ref{fig:process-sequences}(a) counts these paths as logged, and Figure~\ref{fig:process-sequences}(b,c) counts step-to-step transitions.
For Table~\ref{tab:process-dynamics}, immediate repeats of a process are merged (\emph{repeat collapsing}), and when the first delegated role is \texttt{Planning} but the first logged switch names a later process, a leading \texttt{Planning} step is restored (\emph{leading-\texttt{Planning} reconstruction}; \AfourLeadingReconstruction\ such runs for \condAgenticCogWriter).
A path is \emph{cycle-compliant} when the result consists of one or more complete \texttt{Planning}--\texttt{Translating}--\texttt{Reviewing} passes, and returns after \texttt{Reviewing} are counted from this observed order.
\condFixedOrder\ enforces its order through its prompt only, and \AsixCycleCompliantRate\ of its paths are cycle-compliant; the rest skip or repeat a process, for example \texttt{Translating}--\texttt{Reviewing} without \texttt{Planning}.
